sections.title: Introduction
sections.html:
wIA is a multi-engine AI hub: a single chat interface that connects to local models (on your computer or inside the browser) and to the main cloud providers. It is a static web app (HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework and no backend of its own), designed to be fast, private and portable.

  • Privacy first: your chats, projects and settings live only in your browser. There is no backend storing your data.
  • Multi-engine: switch between local and cloud engines without leaving the conversation.
  • No mandatory install: it works by opening a web page; optionally it installs as an app (PWA) and works offline.

sections.title: Getting started
sections.html:
1. Open wIA in your browser (recent Chrome, Edge or similar recommended).
  2. Click the ⚙️ icon (top right) to open Settings and, under Connection, choose the AI engine.
  3. If the engine requires it, enter its API Key or server URL. wIA validates the connection automatically.
  4. Close Settings, type your message and press Enter.

Tip: if you would rather not configure anything, pick WebGPU (Browser); it runs 100% inside your browser, with no keys or servers.

sections.title: AI engines
sections.html:

MistralCloudAPI Key

WebGPU (Browser)Inside the browserNo credentials

API keys: for engines that need one, wIA shows under the key field where to get it, what it looks like and what the service costs. If you paste a key that does not match that engine —another provider's, for instance— it warns you before validating; it is only a warning, you can still validate it.

Each engine remembers its own configuration (model, URL, key and parameters), so you can switch without reconfiguring. The connection is validated when you select an engine and when you save changes.

CORS proxy: when wIA is served with its bundled Node server (or under Plesk), an internal proxy reaches engines that do not allow direct browser calls. On static hosting, wIA detects this and goes straight to providers that do support CORS.

Renaming and duplicating engines

Any engine —built-in or copy— can be renamed from Settings → Connection with the ✎ button: handy for calling “Laptop Ollama” what the app labels “Ollama (Local)”. The name is just a label; the configuration does not move. Leaving the field empty restores the factory name, and engines you never touch keep receiving catalogue updates.

Any engine can be cloned from Settings → Connection, using the ⧉ button next to the selector. The copy takes the name you choose and starts from whatever configuration the original had at that moment —URL, credential, model and parameters— so you only change what differs. From then on they are independent connections: you can keep “Ollama Home” and “Ollama Office” pointing at different machines, or two OpenRouter keys, and switch between them without reconfiguring anything.

Copies are renamed with ✎ and removed with the bin; built-in engines cannot be deleted. When a copy is removed, projects and agents that used it fall back to its original engine instead of pointing at something that no longer exists. WebGPU is not cloneable: it runs inside this very tab, so two entries would share the same runtime.

Official endpoint: commercial engines arrive with the provider’s URL already filled in. If you change it —your own proxy, a different region— or clear it, a “Provider’s official endpoint” line appears under the field with the published address: one click restores it. Remote Ollama proposes none, since there the host is yours.

Signing in with the provider (OAuth)

On OpenRouter, instead of pasting an API Key you can press “Connect with OpenRouter”: wIA sends you to their site, you authorise access and come back with a key of your own account, stored encrypted in this browser. Your password never passes through wIA. It uses OAuth with PKCE (SHA-256), so the authorisation code only works in the tab that started the process.

The other commercial engines still ask for an API Key, and not for lack of support in wIA: OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq and Nvidia publish no OAuth for a third-party website to call their inference API. Google Gemini does support OAuth, but it requires registering a client in Google Cloud declaring the return domain, so it cannot ship preconfigured in an app everyone deploys wherever they like.

Using your ChatGPT subscription instead of API credits

The ChatGPT (subscription) engine does not talk to OpenAI: it connects to a gateway running on your own machine (projects such as openai-oauth or Hermes), which signs in with your ChatGPT account and exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:10531/v1. Start it with npx openai-oauth@latest, leave it running and pick the engine: no key is typed into wIA.

Why it cannot happen inside wIA: that sign-in uses OpenAI’s Codex client flow, which requires a redirect to localhost and calls a backend with no CORS headers. A web page can neither receive that redirect nor make those calls, so the authentication step has to happen outside the browser. Official “Sign in with ChatGPT” for third-party apps, in turn, provides identity (name, email), not inference access on your plan.

Note: these gateways are unofficial projects, unaffiliated with OpenAI. Using your subscription this way is subject to OpenAI’s terms and is your responsibility. The supported alternative is the OpenAI engine with an API Key.

FreeLLMAPI and automatic failover

FreeLLMAPI is a self-hosted gateway that pools the free tiers of dozens of providers behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. wIA only needs its URL and its unified key (freellmapi-…, Keys page of its dashboard). The auto model lets the gateway choose and switch provider when a quota runs out; auto:smart, auto:fast and auto:reliable reorder by capability, speed or reliability. Each message shows with ↪ which provider actually answered.

FreeLLMAPI’s desktop app listens on port 31415 and the Docker installer on 3001; wIA tries both when the URL is the factory one. Without wIA’s own server (node server.js) the gateway only accepts browsers listed in its DASHBOARD_ORIGINS variable.

Automatic failover (Settings → Connection): if the chosen engine fails before answering because of exhausted quota, an outage or a rejected key, wIA tries another engine you have already configured, up to two alternatives. The failing engine is paused (2 min, 10 min, 1 h, 24 h if it repeats; or whatever its Retry-After says) so it is not hit again. Guarantees: it never moves from a local engine to a cloud one or vice versa, never jumps to WebGPU and never retries once text has been received. Free tiers may log queries: with sensitive data, also turn on anonymization.

sections.title: In-browser models (WebGPU)
sections.html:
The WebGPU (Browser) engine runs models directly on your device's GPU/CPU via Transformers.js, without sending anything to a server.

  • Requirements: a browser with WebGPU support (recent Chrome/Edge). Without WebGPU, wIA falls back to WASM (slower).
  • Download and cache: the first time, the model is downloaded from Hugging Face and cached; afterwards it loads instantly and works offline.
  • Adaptive quantisation: wIA picks the precision (q4/q8/fp16) based on your hardware, balancing speed and quality.
  • Web Worker: inference runs on a separate thread so the interface stays responsive.
  • Streaming and cancellation: responses appear token by token and can be stopped.

Loading acceleration

  • Multi-threaded WASM: thanks to cross-origin isolation, the runtime uses several threads (up to 8) plus SIMD, speeding up initialisation and CPU operations.
  • Background preloading: the model starts downloading and initialising as soon as you type, so it is ready when you hit send.
  • «⚡ Prepare model» button: in Settings → Models, downloads and initialises the model on demand.

Using it on mobile

Phones have limited memory (especially iOS, with strict per-tab limits). wIA detects this and: starts with a lightweight model by default, shows a notice in the WebGPU panel and, if you pick a large one, offers to switch to a light model before loading. For maximum quality on the phone, use a cloud engine.

sections.title: Loading speed (WebGPU)
sections.html:
The first time you use an in-browser model there are two costs: the runtime (the engine that runs the model) and the model weights. wIA brings forward everything it can so it does not overlap with your wait:

  • When the app opens with WebGPU active, it prepares the runtime in the background. That cost is fixed and does not depend on the model.
  • When you click the message box, it prepares the runtime if it was not ready yet.
  • When you start typing, it downloads the model while you write.
  • If the model is already cached, it is loaded into memory as soon as the app opens.

It also adapts to your environment: if it detects a slow connection or data saver, it picks the lighter variant of the model (downloads sooner even if it loses some quality); if your GPU lacks shader-f16, it avoids variants that would fail on it; and with no GPU at all it falls back to CPU using every available thread.

In Settings → Connection, with WebGPU selected, the monitor shows how long the last load took, split into runtime and model. If the runtime is slow, that is your connection to the CDN; if the model is slow, that is its size. You can also use "Prepare model" to load it before typing.

sections.title: Vision and images
sections.html:
wIA can analyse images you attach with the 📎 icon. Depending on the engine and model you get:

  • Multimodal models (cloud or WebGPU) that understand image and text together.
  • Vision assistants on WebGPU: image captioning, text reading (OCR) and advanced analysis.
  • Indicative medical models: zero-shot visual classification and a wound classifier that recognises the type (abrasion, bruise, burn, cut, laceration, diabetic/venous/surgical wound, pressure ulcer or normal skin). These are indicative, not diagnostic: when in doubt, consult a healthcare professional.

Vision → chat chain: in Settings → Models (below the selector) you can combine a vision model with a chat model, and enable or disable the chain with its switch. When vision is active, the 👁 icon appears in the message box.

sections.title: Agents
sections.html:
Agents are preconfigured assistants (in the style of GPTs): they combine a name, icon, description, their own system prompt, optionally a specific engine/model, and starters.

  • Open the agent gallery to explore a curated selection and activate them with one click.
  • Create your own with their personality and knowledge base.
  • Export and import agents as JSON to share or back them up.

sections.title: Projects and documents
sections.html:
Projects group chats under a common context. Each project can have:

  • Its own system prompt guiding all its conversations.
  • A knowledge base of documents (including PDF reading), available as permanent reference material for the model.

Switch projects from the selector at the top. The «General» project always exists by default.

Limits: each project document can be up to 4 MB, and each file attached to a message up to 2 MB. Images are resized and re-compressed automatically in your browser before being stored, so they neither exhaust local storage nor bloat every request.

sections.title: Context limit
sections.html:
Every model has a context window: the maximum amount of text it can read at once. wIA works out how much fits and sends what does, always reserving room for the answer.

  • If the conversation is long, the most recent messages are sent and the oldest ones are dropped.
  • If the project knowledge base is large, it is included trimmed, and the model is told so.
  • Your latest question is never dropped, even if on its own it is very long.

When trimming happens, the answer shows a ✂️ label stating what was left out. If you see it often, switch to a model with a larger context or start a new chat.

In-browser models (WebGPU) have the smallest context — several are around 8K tokens — so trimming shows up sooner there.

sections.title: Searching your documents
sections.html:
When a project has large documents, wIA does not send them whole to the model: it searches inside them and sends only the passages related to your question.

  1. The first time it downloads a small search model (about 25-120 MB, kept in cache).
  2. It splits each document and turns it into vectors. That index is stored encrypted in your browser.
  3. On every message it retrieves the passages closest to your question, and only those travel to the model.

When this happens, the answer carries a 🔎 label with how many passages were used. You can turn it off in Settings → Generation, and rebuild the index from there if it ever falls out of sync.

Small documents are not indexed: they fit whole, and building an index for them would only add waiting. If the answer needs something that is not in the passages, the model is instructed to say so rather than make it up.

sections.title: The chat
sections.html:
• Send: Enter. New line: Shift + Enter.
  • Streaming: the reply is written live; you can cancel it.
  • Reasoning: with supported models, wIA shows its «thinking» separately from the answer.
  • Markdown and code: with syntax highlighting and a copy button.
  • Attachments: images and documents via the 📎 icon.
  • Each chat can be exported individually (text/JSON).

Quick fallback when something fails

If a model fails or the provider's credits run out, the error card offers buttons to continue instantly with another model, built from those recently used successfully and your favourites, plus local WebGPU (free, no credits) as a safety net. One click switches engine and retries the message.

sections.title: Quick selectors
sections.html:
From the message box itself you can switch prompt, model or engine without opening Settings:

You typeWhat opens
/Saved prompt library
//Models of the selected engine
///Choose the AI engine
+Queues the order instead of sending it

You can filter by typing after the prefix (for example //qwen or ///groq), navigate with ↑ ↓ and confirm with Enter. The active item is marked as «· current».

sections.title: Web search
sections.html:
wIA can search the internet to answer with current information. When the tool is available, the model uses it automatically if it detects it needs recent data, and you will see the corresponding icon in the message box.

The search combines several sources with layered fallback: real web results (via DuckDuckGo Lite when a proxy is available), DuckDuckGo instant answers and Wikipedia in Spanish and English. This way it returns something useful both with your own server and on static hosting.

sections.title: Order queue
sections.html: If you start a message with the + prefix, instead of being sent it is added to a queue of pending orders. You can queue several and wIA runs them sequentially. The queue persists between sessions and is included in the full backup.

sections.title: Data anonymisation (DLP)
sections.html:
wIA includes a local data protection layer: before sending your prompt to the AI, it replaces sensitive data with consistent placeholders ([Nombre_001], [DNI_001]…).

  • Enable it: with the 🕶️ icon in the message box or from Settings → Anonymisation.
  • Reversible and private: the mapping is stored encrypted per chat (AES-GCM) and the reply is restored only on your screen. The real values never leave the browser.
  • A badge under your message shows how many items were protected.

Recognised data types

Over 20 types are detected: email, phone number, national ID (DNI/NIE/NIF), company tax ID, IBAN, credit card, social security number, passport, physical address, postcode, vehicle plate, IP address, MAC address, dates (possible date of birth), social media handle, API keys and tokens (including JWT), GPS coordinates, policy number, court case and proceedings references, plus dictionaries of personal names and organisations.

Enabling or disabling types

In Settings → Anonymisation all types are listed with a checkbox each, plus an «Enable all» switch. Turn off the ones you do not need (for example dates or IPs if they cause false positives). Your selection is remembered.

sections.title: Privacy and security
sections.html:
• Local inference: with WebGPU, LM Studio or local Ollama, your messages never leave your machine.
  • Everything encrypted locally: API keys, chats, projects, documents and the search index are stored encrypted with AES-GCM, using a non-exportable key that lives in the browser and never leaves it.
  • PIN lock: deters casual access on shared devices. It does not encrypt anything by itself, and needs a secure connection (https or localhost) to be enabled.
  • Incognito mode: disables saving of the current conversation.
  • Anonymisation 🕶️: see the dedicated section.
  • Security headers: the deployment adds cross-origin isolation and headers that harden the app (and enable multi-threaded WASM).

Bear in mind that cloud engines receive your messages on their servers under their own policies; for maximum privacy, use local engines.

sections.title: Backups
sections.html:
Your data lives in the browser and could be cleared if it frees up space. From Settings → Data:

  • Export / Import Settings: preferences and engine configuration only.
  • Export / Import All: a complete copy (projects, agents, chats, order queue and settings) in a single JSON. API keys are excluded for security.

wIA also requests persistent storage to reduce the risk of automatic eviction. Even so, export a copy from time to time.

sections.title: Themes and language
sections.html:
In Settings → Experience you can customise the look and the language.

Themes

  • System (Automatic) — default: follows your operating system's light/dark mode.
  • Tligent (Corporate) — white background, black text and red/grey brand accents.
  • Dark, Light and Vanilla (minimalist).

Language

wIA is available in Spanish and English. By default it detects your browser language. If you pick a specific one in the language selector, that choice is remembered and takes priority over detection. The documentation changes language too.

sections.title: Installation and offline use
sections.html:
wIA is a PWA: from a compatible browser you can install it as an application. Thanks to its service worker, the app shell is stored so it can start offline. Combined with already-cached WebGPU models, you can chat with AI in flight mode.

After a new version is published, you may need to reload once for the service worker to serve the latest one.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.html:
It will not connect to a cloud engine.

Check that the API Key is valid and the URL correct. wIA shows the reason (credentials, URL, network or timeout).

A WebGPU model does not load or is very slow.

Check that your browser has WebGPU enabled; without it, WASM is used, which is slower. Large models take time on the first download and are cached afterwards.

On mobile the tab closes while loading a model.

That is a memory issue. Use a lightweight model (up to ~500 MB) or a cloud engine. wIA warns you and offers to switch automatically.

I lost my chats.

The browser may have cleared storage. Restore from Import All and export copies regularly.

Are the medical image results a diagnosis?

No. They are indicative automatic estimates; any clinical decision belongs to a healthcare professional.
